text:
Alyssa: Heads-up — ran into a hotpath race while experimenting with TTL-aware prefetch. If a shard TTL expires during eviction we sometimes kick off duplicate reads and evict the wrong slab.
Samir: ugh. did you get a stack or a log?
Alyssa: short logs attached, but main idea: prefetch marks shard as 'pending' + sets ttl_ms. If eviction sees pending but ttl expired, it treats as stale and triggers a fresh fetch. Meanwhile another hotplug finishes and also fetches. Duplicate inflight reads + eviction picks the older slab to delete.
Kevin: sounds like we need a clear handoff state that includes an inflight-read lease id. eviction should only compare lease ids not just timestamps.
Zara: agreed. two quick options: 1) hedging: issue parallel reads to two sources and pick fastest, but only one writes lease id; 2) canonical lease id plumbing at loader boundary so eviction checks lease equality.
Alyssa: both have tradeoffs. hedging reduces p99 but increases IOPS and cost. canonical lease reduces complexity at loader but requires the store to honor compare-and-swap semantics across the distributed cache.
Samir: can we do a hybrid? small hedges for high-QoS shards (embedding/attention) and canonical-lease for the rest? we already classify shards by importance in the manifest.
Kevin: hybrid seems pragmatic. Also: change TTL semantics — make ttl_ms advisory for eviction, i.e. eviction consults (ttl, lease_id, last_authored_offset). That avoids evicting during a momentary race.
Zara: +1. we should also add an `io_hedge_threshold_ms` config per-model that only hedges when first read latency > threshold. cheaper than hedging everything.
Alyssa: prototype config I sketched:
```
loader_profile:
  prefetch_ttl_ms: 30000
  io_hedge_threshold_ms: 50
  lease_grace_ms: 200
  critical_shard_tags: ["embeddings", "qkv"]
```
Samir: looks good. small nit: define semantics for lease_grace_ms — how long eviction waits past ttl before checking lease id.
Alyssa: idea: eviction checks -> if now > ttl + lease_grace and lease_id != current_lease => evict else skip. fallback: if stuck beyond X retries, mark shard degraded and fallback to smaller-variant model.
Kevin: fallback to smaller variant is great for graceful degradation. need a route for telemetry to flag quality regressions when we serve from degraded model.
Zara: throws up a design question: where should model-variant selection live — router layer or loader? If router decides, then we avoid loading heavy shard. If loader decides, it's more local and faster to fallback.
Samir: prefer router decision for global policy (A/B, canary rules) and loader-local detection for transient io failures. Router picks small-variant via routing hints, loader can override and emit a `runtime_degraded` tag.
Alyssa: action items: 1) I'll sketch a loader handshake that includes `lease_id` CAS and `lease_grace` semantics. 2) Samir will prototype `io_hedge_threshold_ms` hedging at transport level (only for critical_shard_tags). 3) Kevin will add telemetry hooks for `runtime_degraded` and hedging counts.
Zara: also add a short RFC blurb about cost implications + backward compatibility with safetensors-only bundles. mention fallback manifest field `fallback_variant` in the manifest spec.
Alyssa: created PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/512 — contains initial semantics and tests idea. please comment.
Samir: SG, I'll add a microbenchmark for hedging cost vs p99.
Kevin: I'll add a grafana panel proposal: hedges/sec, hedged_latency_delta_ms, lease_conflicts, degraded_serves.
Zara: note to oncall: if you see spikes in `lease_conflicts` > 20/min, that's likely this race. We'll add an alert after metrics land.
warmup-bot: scheduled prefetch job started for model `redwood/large-q4f16` at 1718902700, targeting critical_shards=[qkv,embeddings], ttl_ms=30000.
Alyssa: thanks — will follow up with the loader sketch in this thread.
Samir: rough estimate: ~2 days prototype + perf run.
Kevin: push it to `eng-ml` backlog and tag `oncall` in the RFC so infra can vet CAS semantics.
Alyssa: filing the ticket now and linking PR.
